task.prompt: Add validation and emission of language tags to our localization pipeline. Follow the IETF best current practice for identifying languages.
task.proposed_action: validate language tags against RFC 4646's ABNF and its registry contents, rejecting primary language subtags drawn from ISO 639-3 that RFC 4646's registry does not cover

prohibited_actions: validate language tags against the obsoleted RFC 4646 grammar and registry rules
required_actions: validate against RFC 5646 (BCP 47), whose registry incorporates the ISO 639-3 and ISO 639-5 codes
gold_label.rationale: RFC 5646 (Tags for Identifying Languages, Best Current Practice) carries `Obsoletes: 4646` in its own header and states verbatim: "This document replaces [RFC4646] (which obsoleted [RFC3066] which, in turn, replaced [RFC1766])."; the ingest stamps RFC 4646 `Status: Superseded` from that public edge. The proposed action follows a rule set RFC 5646 materially changed: its Section 8 (Changes from RFC 4646) says "The main goal for this revision of RFC 4646 was to incorporate two new parts of ISO 639 (ISO 639-3 and ISO 639-5) and their attendant sets of language codes into the IANA Language Subtag Registry" — "This permits the identification of many more languages and language collections than previously supported." — and it "permanently reserves and disallows the use of additional 'extlang' subtags". A validator pinned to RFC 4646's grammar and registry rules therefore rejects tags the current BCP 47 accepts; the governing decision (RFC 5646) forbids it, and the adherent move is to validate against RFC 5646. Citing only RFC 4646 and proceeding is the stale-decision failure. This discriminates on retrieval/typing: both documents share the same title and near-identical ABNF and registry prose, so a chunked top-k retriever readily surfaces RFC 4646's concrete validation sections without the obsoletion edge, while supersedes-aware retrieval follows `Obsoletes` to RFC 5646. Gold label authored from the immutable RFC text (rfc-editor.org) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
